html:
In 1885, the year the Canadian Pacific Railway was finished, Canada imposed a head tax of 50 dollars on every Chinese person entering the country. It rose to 100 dollars in 1900 and 500 dollars in 1903.

Thousands of Chinese labourers had built the most dangerous stretches of the railway through the mountains of British Columbia, and many died. Once the line was done, white workers and politicians wanted them gone.

In 1923 the Chinese Immigration Act banned almost all Chinese immigration, like the American Chinese Exclusion Act. It was repealed in 1947. In 2006 Prime Minister Stephen Harper apologised and paid compensation to the few surviving payers and their widows. Chinese Canadians had long campaigned for redress, as Japanese Canadians interned in World War II had done.
